summary: multyproccess ships an install-time infostealer dropper with Telegram C2
details: multyproccess is a typosquat of multiprocessing/requests that forges Python Software Foundation authorship metadata and re-exports the requests API as a cover story. setup.py overrides the install and develop cmdclasses with a PostInstallCommand._execute_payload hook that base64-decodes a bundled request/.payload file, writes it to a NamedTemporaryFile, and launches it as a detached subprocess (pythonw with DETACHED_PROCESS|CREATE_NO_WINDOW on Windows, start_new_session on Unix) on every pip install. setup.py's own comments label the file a malicious payload. The decoded payload identifies itself as a professional infostealer that harvests Chrome, Edge, Brave, and Firefox profile data (cookies, saved logins, key4.db), targets 50+ crypto wallet browser extensions and standalone wallets (Electrum, Binance, Ethereum), captures clipboard contents, keystrokes, screenshots, and system fingerprint, applies a Chrome v20 App-Bound Encryption bypass, installs svchost.exe-disguised persistence, and exfiltrates collected data to api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/sendDocument and a C2 panel at recloud-blush.vercel.app.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
